sections.html:
County government for Leavenworth County is here, along the Missouri River's west bank, roughly 25 miles northwest of downtown Kansas City. U.S. 73 and K-92 meet in town, and the metro area counts it as a member. Of the 24.06 square miles inside city limits, Fort Leavenworth occupies the northern half, and Lansing borders the south.

Four small creeks run east through town to the river: Quarry Creek, Corral Creek, Three Mile Creek and Five Mile Creek. Your house could be near the post, the river bluffs or one of those creeks, and buyers ask different questions about drainage and grading depending on which.

Leavenworth, founded in 1854, holds the title of first incorporated city in the Kansas Territory. It grew south of Fort Leavenworth, which began in 1827 as Cantonment Leavenworth under Colonel Henry Leavenworth. On April 3, 1858, the Leavenworth Constitution for the state of Kansas was adopted in the city, though the federal government never approved it.

That age shows in the housing, and older houses raise familiar questions about wiring, plumbing, sewer lines and foundations.

sections.h2: Military jobs and moving on a schedule
sections.html:
The military anchors the local economy. Fort Leavenworth employs roughly 5,600 people, making it the largest employer, with Leavenworth Public Schools and the federal VA's Eastern Kansas Health Care System behind it. Other large employers include Northrop Grumman, Central Plains Consolidated Accounts and Leavenworth Federal Penitentiary.

Posts and federal offices mean steady turnover. Orders and transfers can force a sale on somebody else's schedule, and a quick close beats a long listing in that spot.

Leavenworth USD 453 covers most addresses, with four elementary schools, one middle school, Leavenworth High School and a virtual school. The post has its own district, Fort Leavenworth USD 207, and a sliver on the south edge falls under Lansing USD 469. Look up the district for your address, since buyers ask.

No city in Kansas of this size is without fixed-route public transit except Leavenworth. RideLV, an app-based on-demand service run by The Guidance Center with the Kansas City Area Transportation Authority, began in April 2023. Intercity trains and buses leave from Kansas City, Missouri. Most households drive, so a garage and off-street parking help a listing.

Hot, humid summers and colder, drier winters define the year. Roofs and cooling systems get a real workout. On average January is coldest, July hottest and June wettest. The record high is 114 F in August, and May's record is 103 F, so roofs and air conditioners work hard.

With several creeks crossing the city on their way to the river, drainage deserves a look. Buyers and inspectors check downspouts, grading and basement moisture. If you know of past water in the basement, say so up front and keep any repair receipts, because a buyer who finds it later will ask for a lower price. Fresh paint over a stain tends to draw more questions than an honest note about what was fixed. Swings between freezing winters and hot summers are also hard on masonry and foundations.

Under the Rental Registration program, every rented single-family house, multi-family building and rented unit inside an owner-occupied dwelling has to register. The rules are in Sections 10-568 through 10-572 of the city code.

  • Filing is with the City Clerk at 100 N. 5th Street and costs $20 per property when the title name is the same.
  • Properties titled under different names need separate registrations.
  • Living more than 40 miles away means appointing an agent within 40 miles, who shares responsibility for upkeep and code compliance.
  • Report any change to the registered information in writing within 30 days.
  • Hotels, bed and breakfasts with a state permit, churches, nursing facilities, jails and housing authority units are exempt.

Because registration follows the name on the title, a sale changes it. The new owner generally registers separately, and you should notify the city. The Rental Property Coordinator at 913-364-5840 answers questions.

The county treasurer collects what Leavenworth County bills. Taxes are paid in arrears: December 20 for the first half, then May 10 of the following year for the second.

Tax stepLeavenworth County date
Statements mailedNovember 1 to December 15
First half dueDecember 20
Second half dueMay 10 of the next year
Second-half noticesNone mailed
Online payments openNov 1 to Dec 20 and Jan 1 to May 10

Because no second-half notice is mailed, sellers who count on a reminder can miss the date. Interest follows a missed date, and the title company will want unpaid tax cleared at closing. For a spring closing, make sure the second half is covered.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Leavenworth County
sections.html:
Go to the Leavenworth County Register of Deeds at 300 Walnut Street, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., or call 913-684-0424.

Warranty deeds, transfer on death deeds and quit claim deeds all go on record there. Free title research is not something this recording office can offer. The register's site also has a property fraud page for owners. An inherited house still recorded in the late owner's name will need that record fixed before closing, and the title company will say so.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell?
sections.html:
Owners here pick between an agent listing, a private sale and a cash purchase.

  • Listing reaches the widest pool of buyers, though a lender will insist that inspection items get handled.
  • A sale by owner works when you have the time and understand the disclosure and contract steps.
  • Cash suits houses needing work, vacant rentals, inherited property and anyone up against a deadline.

We buy Leavenworth houses as is, older downtown homes and tired rentals included. Request an offer, set it against a listing's net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, and choose by your own timeline.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like here
sections.html:
Start by sending the address and telling us whether tenants live there. We view the property in its current state, with no cleaning or repair expected, and send a written offer. Accept, decline or compare it with a listing.

Once you accept, a title company searches the record, drafts the deed and pays any open property tax out of what you receive. The closing date is yours to choose, which helps when orders, a new job or an estate drives your calendar. Bring photo ID, keys and any paperwork on the roof, sewer line or foundation. With a rental, add the lease and the registration record.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental in Leavenworth before selling it?
faqs.a: Registration applies for as long as you own a rented house, at $20 per property under one title name. After a sale, notify the city within 30 days. A buyer who rents the house registers on their own.

faqs.q: When are Leavenworth County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 for the first half, May 10 of the following year for the second. Statements go out November 1 through December 15, and nobody mails a second-half notice.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Leavenworth?
faqs.a: The Leavenworth County Register of Deeds, 300 Walnut Street, 913-684-0424. Warranty, transfer on death and quit claim deeds are all recorded there.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Leavenworth house?
faqs.a: Mostly Leavenworth USD 453. The post is in Fort Leavenworth USD 207 and a southern edge is in Lansing USD 469, so check your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leavenworth house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take the house as is, so foundation, roof or code trouble can wait until after closing. Lenders for conventional buyers usually insist on repairs first.
